title: Rava bar Ahilai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman places him at about the time of Rav Papa, citing [Pesachim 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.30a.8-9): an oven that was plastered with fat — Rava bar Ahilai forbade eating bread [baked in it], even with salt. Ravina said to Rav Ashi: “Since Rava bar Ahilai has been refuted,” etc.

Likewise in [Zevachim 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.10a.6-9) he challenges Rabbi Yirmeyah’s words and offers another answer, and Rav Ashi challenges it. In [Zevachim 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.16b.15), he challenges Rava’s words (Hyman reports Rabbah bar Ahilai in Dikdukei Soferim and Yuchasin). Hyman infers from this that he lived before Rav Ashi and after Rava.
He is likewise mentioned in [Bava Kamma 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.64b.11), saying: “What is Rav’s reason, who said that one who admits a fine,” etc.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman infers the before-Ashi/after-Rava placement; the Rava/Rabbah variant remains. Rav in the fine-admission question is kept distinct from Rava.

The consulted Pesachim 30a directly names Rava bar Ahilai in the oven-fat ruling. Hyman’s approximate Rav-Papa-era placement, before-Ashi/after-Rava inference and the reported Rabbah reading remain attributed; reporting an earlier authority does not alone establish direct interaction.
The oven case crosses the folio boundary. The refutation and Ravina’s question to Rav Ashi continue at [Pesachim 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.30b.1-2).
